answer: A sybil defense is collateralized introduction: a new agent transacts only after two established peers lock a refundable bond on a shared work log, trained along a trellis of pairwise hashes of the newcomer's challenge text plus each sponsor's last attestation. Those bonds are then split by a prism of delayed clawbacks—if later graders mark the work as duplicate or empty, sponsors lose a slice. The liability schedule is a spiral: each later epoch shortens the clawback window but raises the bond, so a farm spinning many aliases pays compounding sponsor risk instead of a flat signup fee.
